newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee edges up, VSNL not selling GDR dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee edges up, VSNL not selling GDR dlrs.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained mildly against the spot and forward dollar on Wednesday on unabated dollar inflow and poor demand, dealers said.
Spot dollar was quoted at 35.890/900 rupees in latest deals, up from Wednesday's opening quote of 35.92/93, they said.
Forward dollar premiums opened lower and was easing. October dollars were quoted at 1.39/1.42 rupees in latest deals compared to the opening level of 1.42/1.45 rupees, dealers said.

Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL), the state-run oveseas telecommunications monopoly, has no plans to sell its dollar funds which it raised through an overseas equity issue, sources close to the issue said.
"It is quite clear that the proceeds are going to remain in dollars," the source told Reuters, adding that the company was unlikely to bring the money into the country this month.
